items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: spent some time listening to Clifford Brown records

ctx.x: Why is it a lost art these days? You’ve got so many music schools now where you can go and learn this craft.

Yeah. But we have all kinds of written music, don’t we. We have a lot of big band stuff and it’s all written out. Phil Woods waxes poetic on this point. But there are very few schools in which they take the time to teach the craft of playing in a small ensemble, okay. Say one say the size of the one that we recorded with today, or smaller. You know, very few teach the responsibility of functioning in those ensembles. I have a little question and answer game that I play with every clinic group I work for. I say,…
Yeah, in high school they don’t get much chance to do a small combo, or how many instructors in high school really know how that goes anyway.
